metas.name: 1 barely visible left dot - around David
metas.note: This very small dot to the left is common north and west of David.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: 1 bottom stain - east
metas.note: A small cluster of dirt on the car can be found on the eastern road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: 1 dot right - Northwest
metas.note: This car with a small stain to the right is only found between Gualaca District and Changuinola.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: 1 or 2 left dots - central
metas.note: In a lot of central Panama, the Google car will have either one or two black dots visible on the front.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Banana plantations - around Changuinola
metas.note: The region around Changuinola is filled with banana plantations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Bike lane - Pesé - Chitre
metas.note: Road 50 is the only one in Panama to have a bike lane, from Pesé to Chitre
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Cerro Trinidad - West of Capira
metas.note: Cerro Trinidad is a recognizable mountain with exposed rocky slopes west of Capira.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Divided grainy Highway - Highway 9
metas.note: Highway 9 going from Panama City north to Colón is a divided concrete highway. The road is visibly grainy and has a lot of tar lines. The landscape is lush and hilly.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Divided Highway + Barù volcano - Road 41
metas.note: Highway 41 is one of the 6 divided highways of the country. It is pretty easy to recognize because it is the one going to the Barù volcano, so it is sloping and the volcano is visible 90% of the time.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Finca - Northwest
metas.note: Cities of Changuinola, Torres Bluff and Guabito name their suburbs the same way : “(Finca) Las XX” ,“XX” being the suburb number. They are the only cities where it is done that way.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: flat, brown or orange soil - around Aguadulce
metas.note: The region around Aguadulce is relatively flat and features a lot of agricultural fields along with very brown or orange soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Flat, open fields - around David
metas.note: The area around David is very flat, with lots of fairly open fields. Usually, mountains will be visible to the north and northeast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Freshly Paved - Road 407
metas.note: Road 407 from Boca Chica to the junction with the panamerican highway has been concreted recently. Some parts of it are still dirt and under construction while some are concreted with dotted road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: High altitude + dry mountains - Ngäbe-Buglé province
metas.note: The main covered road in the Ngäbe-Buglé province is very high-altitude and almost above the clouds. The surrounding mountains tend to be quite dry, and the altitude makes for many stunning views.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Horizontal plate - western
metas.note: Many poles in the western provinces will have horizontal plates attached to them. However, if one of these is accompanied by an eastern vertical plate, the eastern plate takes precedence.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Lowered Antenna - mostly Colon and Panama City
metas.note: The antenna can be seen folded down, most commonly in Colón and Panamá provinces, and occasionally in the city of David.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Lush green + overcast -  road going to Changuinola
metas.note: The road going to Changuinola features a lush and green hilly landscape. The weather is cloudy or overcast on the entire road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Meseta de Chorcha - east of David
metas.note: On a small stretch of the panamerican highway east of David, a rocky formation, Meseta de Chorcha, can be seen. It is a very distinct elevation point and is unique in this region.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: MOP sticker - Central, rarely west
metas.note: MOP-sticker -The sticker is always black and small -Only in these 5 states, but for Coclé and Veraguas there by far mostly in the south of the state and in Chiriqui not that common -The highway in southern Veraguas almost has this sticker on every sign
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: MOP sticker big - Max. east
metas.note: MOP-paint -This again reads ‘MOP’ with its logo and all. This time it has a lot of text above the logo -The difference, obviously, is that it's black paint (not a sticker) and it's very big -Only on the green part of the CA-1 in Darién but this time it's on most of the signs along the road
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Phone Code 2 - Capital & east
metas.note: Phone codes starting with 2 are found in Panama City and the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Phone Code 4 - Colon Province
metas.note: Phone codes starting with 4 are found in Colon.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Phone Code 7 - Bocas del Toro & Chiriquí
metas.note: Phone codes starting with 7 are found in the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Phone Code 9 - central states
metas.note: Phone codes starting with 9 are found in Coclé, Herrera, Los Santos & Veraguas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Red dot on the right - Panamá Oeste & road 2
metas.note: This small red spot can mostly be found in Panamá Oeste and on the road 2 going from southern Los Santos province to the Verguas province. Note: Road 2 is the only divided road with this car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Sunset - South of Tonosi
metas.note: Sunset coverage can be found in southern Panama on a small road south of Tonosi. The more south you go, the lower the sun.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Taxi Code 1 - Bocas del Toro
metas.note: Just like Colombian taxis, taxis in Panama are yellow and have the name of the city/province labeled on them. It is sometimes hard to read Panama Taxis plates, especially the name of the province/city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.note: Just like Colombian taxis, taxis in Panama are yellow and have the name of the city/province labeled on them. It is sometimes hard to read Panama Taxis plates, especially the name of the province/city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Thin yellow plate - mostly Colón Province
metas.note: Thin yellow plates, vertical or horizontal, with a visible black border are most common in the Colón Province.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Triangle dots - Southwest of Panama City
metas.note: This triangle of dots on the front right of the car is common southwest of the capital.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Tropical landscape - around Colón and Panama City
metas.note: Green tropical landscapes with palm trees and very tall grass are common around Colón and Panama City.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Vertical Plate - eastern
metas.note: The eastern provinces often have tall vertical plates that can be yellow or white. They are commonly attached to poles by black zip ties.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Volcanic rock - North of David
metas.note: Volcanic rocks that are either scattered on the ground, or built into rock walls, are common north of David.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Volcanic rock + dry + pines - Northeast of Volcán
metas.note: A mountainous landscape with pine trees, volcanic rocks, dry grass, and gravel roads can be found northeast of Volcán.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Warehouses & rundown multi - Colon
metas.note: Colón features a lot of warehouses and rundown multi-storey buildings.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: White high rise buildings - Panama City
metas.note: Panama City can be recognised by the large number of white high-rise buildings.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Wind turbines - around Penonome
metas.note: Northern: in the mountains, southern: in a flat area
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Yellow pole socks - around Gatún
metas.note: Yellow pole socks can be found near the Panama Canal, around the town of Gatún.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
